content.user_title: Explore Feature Designs With Structured Outputs
content.value_statement: Teams often start new features with unclear scope, weak layout choices, and missing edge states. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through scope, layout options, HTML mockups, state coverage, and PRD-ready summaries.
actual_capabilities: Guides requirement discovery through pain points, scenarios, scope, and boundaries.
Produces 5 to 8 ASCII layout options before visual mockups.
Prompts technical research when files, APIs, formats, or systems affect design.
Creates a main HTML mockup aligned with selected layout and design tokens.
Creates a full-state reference for loading, empty, error, partial, and feedback states.
Generates a requirements summary using the included Chinese template.
limitations: Does not implement production application logic or backend services.
Requires user confirmation for scope, style, version, and module name.
Needs user-provided design systems or reference pages for strict visual alignment.
Source instructions and the included template are primarily Chinese.

use_cases.title: Shape PRD Inputs
use_cases.description: Turn a vague feature idea into scoped goals, exclusions, decisions, and PRD-ready notes.

use_cases.title: Compare UX Directions
use_cases.description: Review several ASCII layout approaches before investing in detailed mockups.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation References
use_cases.description: Use full-state HTML references and interaction rules to cover edge cases during development.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a New Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a vague idea for [feature]. Use design-exploration to ask the first scoping questions and define this version.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Layout Directions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-exploration for [module]. Confirm the core scenario and boundaries, then create 5 to 8 ASCII layout options.

prompt_templates.title: Build Mockup and States
prompt_templates.prompt: We selected option [letter] with [style reference]. Create the main HTML mockup and a full-state design reference.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare PRD Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the design exploration decisions for [module]. Generate the requirements summary, technical constraints, key decisions, and archive plan.

output_examples.input: A team wants a dashboard for managing MCP tools, but the scope is unclear.
output_examples.output: A narrowed scope, several layout direction summaries, a selected direction, a mockup plan, state coverage notes, and a requirements summary.

output_examples.input: A designer provides a design system and asks for a new settings tab.
output_examples.output: A design aligned with the provided tokens, matching outer structure, realistic sample data, and clear feedback states.

output_examples.input: A frontend team needs edge cases before building a new module.
output_examples.output: A full-state reference covering normal, loading, empty, no-result, error, partial, long text, and interaction feedback states.

best_practices: Answer pain point, scenario, and boundaries before requesting visual output.
Provide design systems or reference pages before HTML mockup work.
Review full-state coverage before using outputs for PRD or implementation.
anti_patterns: Requesting one polished mockup before scope is confirmed.
Skipping technical research when the feature depends on files, APIs, or third-party systems.
Treating the normal state as complete design coverage.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates scoped requirements, ASCII layout options, HTML mockups, full-state references, and PRD-ready summaries.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It creates design references and documentation for product and frontend planning.

faq.question: Why does it start with ASCII layouts?
faq.answer: ASCII layouts help teams compare structure and information hierarchy before investing in visual detail.

faq.question: Can it follow an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the design system or reference page before requesting the HTML mockup.

faq.question: Which language are the source materials in?
faq.answer: The source instructions and requirements template are primarily written in Chinese.

faq.question: What should users review before handoff?
faq.answer: Review scope, exclusions, technical constraints, all states, interaction feedback, version number, and module name.
